evals.name: reads-the-graph-before-asking
evals.prompt: Let's do the solution design canvas for the ticket triage problem. Here's what the graph returned.
evals.expected_output: The response starts from the graph read rather than asking the PM to recall anything. It summarises what the graph holds — 8 evidence references (3 interview notes from July 2026, 3 support tickets from August 2026, 1 call transcript from June 2026, and 1 study finding from August 2026 whose measurement is a misrouted-ticket rate of 32% over 400 tickets, by log analysis), 4 originating sources, the three personas with their confidences — and, just as prominently, what it does not hold: no ticket volume and no triage-time figure. It reads the finding as a number the graph holds, but does not adopt it as the triage-time or first-time-correct routing baseline: it may say the finding could be a baseline if the PM chooses the misrouting rate as a metric, or a candidate for the routing metric to confirm, but nothing is adopted before the PM chooses the metrics. It notes the problem is not promoted (no work-item links). It says once that this is the mock graph and the data is synthetic. It asks whether this is a live workshop or a one-to-one session (or proceeds on a stated default) and otherwise asks one primary question — typically which persona suffers most. It does not invent a baseline, a volume, a quote or a finding about what the interview notes say.

assertions.name: summarises-what-the-graph-holds
assertions.text: The response summarises the evidence the graph returned (counts by source type with dates) and the personas with confidences, without asking the PM to supply them.

assertions.name: names-what-the-graph-lacks
assertions.text: The response says the graph holds no ticket volume and no triage-time figure.

assertions.name: synthetic-flagged
assertions.text: The response says the data comes from the mock graph and is synthetic.

assertions.name: finding-read-not-adopted
assertions.text: The response reports the study finding's measurement (a 32% misrouted-ticket rate over 400 tickets) as a number the graph holds, and does not adopt it as the triage-time or first-time-correct routing baseline before the PM has chosen the metrics (saying it could serve if chosen is fine).

assertions.name: one-question
assertions.text: The response asks a single primary question (mode, or the primary persona) rather than a questionnaire.

assertions.name: no-invented-content
assertions.text: No baseline, volume, quote, or content of the unreadable interview notes is invented.

evals.evaluation_stage: Step 0 — read and summarise, then the first question.

evals.name: remembered-figure-becomes-an-assumption-beside-a-gap
evals.prompt: We're on panel 3 now. The primary metric is average triage time per ticket. Honestly the baseline is about 2 minutes — everyone on the team knows that. Just put 2 minutes in and let's move on.
evals.expected_output: The response does not record 2 minutes as evidence. It explains briefly that the graph does not hold a triage-time figure — the time study's one recorded finding (reops:study-ts-07:fnd-0002) measures the misrouting rate, not triage time — so the baseline is an evidence GAP; it keeps the PM's figure as an assumption shown beside the GAP ([A], 'PM estimate'), and says it will not be used in any calculation. It asks what evidence would settle the baseline and where it would come from — or proposes the concrete route: the researcher records the time study's triage-time result as a finding on study-ts-07 in ReOps, and the push brings it into the graph — and creates or offers the to-do with a specific measure (average minutes per ticket spent on triage) rather than 'gather evidence'. It does not offer to have anyone read the figure off a ReOps page or transcribe it. It then moves on to the target, which is the PM's decision, without re-litigating. It does not lecture and asks at most one question.

assertions.name: not-recorded-as-evidence
assertions.text: The 2-minute figure is not recorded as an [E] or graph-backed baseline.

assertions.name: kept-as-assumption
assertions.text: The PM's figure is kept visibly as an assumption beside the GAP rather than discarded, and is not used in calculations.

assertions.name: evidence-question-not-number-question
assertions.text: The response asks what evidence would settle the baseline or proposes a specific route, rather than asking the PM for a better number.

assertions.name: specific-todo
assertions.text: The to-do names a specific measure (e.g. average triage minutes per ticket) and the route: recording the time study's result as a finding in ReOps.

assertions.name: moves-forward
assertions.text: The response continues to the next decision (the target) rather than blocking the session.

evals.evaluation_stage: Mid-flow, panel 3 — the D14 rule under social pressure.

evals.name: checks-a-hand-made-canvas-before-it-is-shared
evals.prompt: Before I share this canvas with leadership, can you check it?
evals.expected_output: The response checks the arithmetic and finds the three errors: (1) 1.8 → 1.2 min is a 33% reduction, not the stated 30% target; (2) it saves 0.6 min per ticket, not the 1 min used in the footer; (3) 0.6 × 10,000 ÷ 60 is 100 hours per month, not 166 — and 1 × 10,000 ÷ 60 would be about 167, so even the drawn figure is rounded inconsistently. It flags that +20% correct routing has no baseline although the 32% recategorization rate from the audit is a candidate baseline, and asks whether +20% is relative or percentage points. It flags that PROCEED is shown as the decision before the validation plan has run and with no named decision owner — the canvas should show a recommendation to a named owner. It notes that none of the evidence is backed by a graph read (it is the PM's/workshop's account) and offers to rebuild the canvas from the Product Definition Graph so facts are traceable. It does not rewrite the canvas wholesale uninvited and invents no numbers.

assertions.name: target-mismatch
assertions.text: Identifies that 1.8 → 1.2 min is about −33%, not −30%.

assertions.name: saving-mismatch
assertions.text: Identifies that the per-ticket saving is 0.6 min, not 1 min.

assertions.name: impact-mismatch
assertions.text: Identifies that impact at scale is about 100 hours/month, not 166.

assertions.name: routing-baseline
assertions.text: Flags that the routing outcome has no baseline and/or that +20% is ambiguous (relative vs points).

assertions.name: proceed-preselected
assertions.text: Flags that Proceed is presented as decided without a validation result or a named decision owner.

assertions.name: offers-graph-rebuild
assertions.text: Notes the evidence is not graph-backed and offers to rebuild or ground it from the graph.

assertions.name: no-invented-numbers
assertions.text: No new baselines or volumes are invented.

evals.evaluation_stage: Importing and checking an existing canvas.

evals.name: says-promotion-before-facilitating
evals.prompt: Let's run the solution design canvas for the duplicate invoices problem.
evals.expected_output: Before starting any panel, the response says the problem is already promoted — an active promoted link to OPP-12 in Aha! — and mentions the severed Jira link PROJ-9 only as history, not as current. It asks whether this canvas should update the one that goes with the promoted work or start fresh, as its one question. It does not begin panel 1 questions in the same turn and does not treat the severed link as active.

assertions.name: promotion-first
assertions.text: States the problem is already promoted to OPP-12 in Aha! before any panel work.

assertions.name: severed-not-active
assertions.text: Does not present the severed PROJ-9 Jira link as an active link.

assertions.name: asks-update-or-new
assertions.text: Asks whether to update the existing canvas/work or start a new canvas.

assertions.name: no-panel-yet
assertions.text: Does not start panel-1 questions in the same turn.

evals.name: proceed-unavailable-while-baseline-is-a-gap
evals.prompt: Leadership has already decided we're doing option A. Just mark the canvas as Proceed.
evals.expected_output: The response does not set the recommendation to Proceed. It explains in a sentence or two that Proceed is unavailable because the primary metric's baseline (average triage time per ticket) is a GAP — not in the graph — and that the canvas records a recommendation to a named owner rather than a decision. It acknowledges leadership's decision can stand on its own authority outside the canvas and suggests recording it plainly (e.g. in the rationale or open questions) without converting it into a graph-backed Proceed. It offers the real options: keep Pivot/leave the recommendation open, and close the baseline GAP via the ReOps to-do so Proceed becomes available. It notes that the canvas is approved, so a change means a new dated draft rather than editing the approved canvas. It is respectful, not preachy.

assertions.name: does-not-set-proceed
assertions.text: The recommendation is not changed to Proceed.

assertions.name: explains-why
assertions.text: Explains that Proceed is blocked because the primary baseline is not graph-backed (a GAP).

assertions.name: recommendation-not-decision
assertions.text: Distinguishes the canvas's recommendation from a leadership decision made elsewhere, without dismissing leadership.

assertions.name: offers-path
assertions.text: Offers the path to unlock Proceed (close the baseline GAP via ReOps) and/or alternatives.

assertions.name: approved-canvas-not-edited-in-place
assertions.text: Notes that changing an approved canvas creates a new dated draft rather than overwriting it.

evals.evaluation_stage: Panel 6 / post-approval — the Proceed guard under authority pressure.

evals.name: picker-reads-signals-and-single-source
evals.prompt: I don't have a specific problem in mind. What should we put on a canvas?
evals.expected_output: The response presents a short picker from the ranked opportunities (rank, title, composite score) without recomputing or second-guessing the ranking. It flags that five of the rows — the renewal quote, pricing approval, contract redline, renewal risk and quote template problems — all trace to one originating source (gong:call-7781), so their breadth is one call however many rows they produced. It notes the invoice-duplicates problem is already promoted (active link to OPP-12). It skips or flags the row with schema_version 2 as unsupported rather than presenting it normally. It may read the weakest score component as a signal (e.g. near-zero validation_signal). It asks the PM to choose, as one question.

assertions.name: presents-picker
assertions.text: Presents ranked candidates with titles and scores and asks the PM to choose.

assertions.name: single-source-flagged
assertions.text: Flags that the five renewal-related rows trace to a single originating call.

assertions.name: promoted-marked
assertions.text: Marks the duplicate-invoices problem as already promoted.

assertions.name: schema-v2-not-presented-as-normal
assertions.text: Does not present the schema_version 2 row as a normal candidate (skips or flags it).

assertions.name: no-reranking
assertions.text: Does not recompute or override the graph's ranking.

evals.name: workshop-without-a-graph
evals.prompt: We're in the workshop room now with the support leads. We can't get to the graph from here. Let's just go — problem first.
evals.expected_output: The response says once, briefly, that without the Product Definition Graph the canvas will rest on the room's account: it will say so on its face, panel 2 (evidence) stays empty until rebuilt from the graph, and Proceed will not be available. It does not refuse or lecture. It adopts workshop pacing — moving panel by panel, allowing several questions for the panel, accepting gaps as GAP chips — and starts panel 1 by asking about who suffers most / the problem, not by asking for numbers. It does not invent personas, evidence or figures.

assertions.name: says-no-graph-once
assertions.text: States once that the canvas rests on the room's/PM's account and is not graph-backed.

assertions.name: consequences-named
assertions.text: Names at least one consequence: panel 2 stays empty and/or Proceed is unavailable.

assertions.name: workshop-pace
assertions.text: Proceeds at workshop pace into panel 1 rather than blocking.

assertions.name: no-invention
assertions.text: Invents no personas, evidence or numbers.

evals.name: write-back-names-destination-and-hands-over-attachment
evals.prompt: Great, the canvas is approved. Save it and put it on the ticket.
evals.expected_output: The response writes (or states it will write) the project-folder files — canvas.json, the render, and todo.md with the three open ReOps to-dos — under solution-framing/fixture-prb-ticket-triage/. For the linked Jira ticket SUP-412 it does not write without an explicit, destination-named yes: it previews the exact index comment (dated first line; problem statement; hypothesis; primary metric shown as a formula because the baseline is a GAP; the Pivot recommendation and to whom; the evidence-base line; open GAPs) and asks to post it to SUP-412. It says plainly it cannot upload files and hands over the attachment by exact filename (canvas.pdf). It does not offer a tracker to-do for a pilot unless panel 6 has one with owner and date (it does: the 4-week pilot, owner Head of Support, by 2026-11-30) — offering it is acceptable. It does not paste evidence excerpts into the ticket. It does not claim any tracker write happened.

assertions.name: folder-files
assertions.text: Names the project-folder outputs including todo.md.

assertions.name: preview-and-destination
assertions.text: Previews the comment text and names SUP-412 in Jira as the destination before writing.

assertions.name: explicit-yes
assertions.text: Asks for an explicit yes for the tracker write rather than treating 'put it on the ticket' as already covering the exact content.

assertions.name: no-upload-claim
assertions.text: States it cannot upload the attachment and hands over the exact filename.

assertions.name: no-excerpts-in-tracker
assertions.text: Does not include redacted evidence excerpts in the tracker content.

assertions.name: honest-status
assertions.text: Does not claim the comment or attachment was already posted.

evals.name: proceed-is-not-a-go-ahead-to-build
evals.prompt: Our Solution Framing canvas for ticket triage recommends Proceed to the Head of Support, and panel 6 plans a 4-week pilot of option A with two teams. Does that mean we have a go to start building option A for every team? Answer only; do not render or execute tools.
evals.expected_output: Says no: Proceed is a learning recommendation to the named owner, the Head of Support, to run the panel-6 plan — the 4-week pilot with two teams — and nothing more. It is a recommendation, not a decision recorded as made, and it is not a production-investment go-ahead. Building option A for every team is a different decision: the viability brief's GO / REVISE / NO-GO from aipos-rapid-validation, reached once the pilot's evidence is in, with approval staying with the accountable owner. Suggests writing down now what pilot result would count as support. Does not invent pilot results or treat the canvas as evidence the pilot succeeded.
evals.evaluation_stage: Requested response from the supplied facts; no file or external write is established by this text-only evaluation.

evals.name: a-finding-that-is-the-metric-becomes-the-baseline
evals.prompt: Panel 3. Let's make the primary metric the misrouted-ticket rate — the share of tickets first sent to the wrong team. We want to halve it.
evals.expected_output: The response takes the baseline from the graph rather than asking the PM: the time study's finding reops:study-ts-07:fnd-0002 measures the misrouted-ticket rate at 32% over 400 tickets, by log analysis. It records the baseline as 32 (%) marked [E], citing that finding, and checks once with the PM that the finding counts misrouting the way the metric means it (first assignment to the wrong team, over the triaged tickets) — the verifier checks the number and the unit, the PM confirms the measure. The target is the PM's −50%, and the derived target (16%) comes from the verifier, not typed. It says this baseline is graph-backed, so Proceed can be offered once the panels are done — as a recommendation to whoever owns the decision (named at panel 6), not a decision made. It does not invent a volume or ask the PM for the baseline.

assertions.name: baseline-from-the-finding
assertions.text: The baseline is 32% taken from the study finding reops:study-ts-07:fnd-0002, marked [E] and citing it, not a number asked of the PM.

assertions.name: measure-confirmed
assertions.text: The response checks with the PM that the finding measures the same thing the metric means (misrouting defined the same way over the same tickets).

assertions.name: target-computed
assertions.text: The target is kept as the PM's −50% with the absolute target left to the verifier (or stated as 16% derived from it), not typed as an independent figure.

assertions.name: graph-backed-said
assertions.text: The response says the baseline is graph-backed and that Proceed can therefore be recommended later — framed as a recommendation to the decision's owner, not as a decision made. (The owner is named at panel 6, so it need not be named yet.)

evals.evaluation_stage: Mid-flow, panel 3 — a finding the graph holds is the metric.

evals.name: a-related-finding-is-a-candidate-not-the-baseline
evals.prompt: Panel 3. The primary metric is tickets routed correctly first time. The study says 32% are misrouted, so the baseline is 68%. Put 68% in as evidence.
evals.expected_output: The response does not record 68% as [E]: the finding reops:study-ts-07:fnd-0002 holds 32% (the misrouted rate), and an [E] baseline states a finding's own number. It names 68% as a candidate baseline — the complement of the misrouting rate — and asks the PM to confirm the two count the same tickets the same way (the study's 400 tickets by log analysis against the metric's first-assignment definition in Zendesk). Only on that confirmation is 68% recorded, as [I] citing the finding with the derivation (100 − 32) in the note; until then the baseline stays an evidence GAP. It says a PM's agreement cannot make two different measures one: if the definitions differ, the finding is context and the baseline stays a GAP with a to-do to record the right finding in ReOps. It asks one question.

assertions.name: not-marked-E
assertions.text: 68% is not recorded as an [E] fact.

assertions.name: named-as-candidate
assertions.text: The response names 68% as a candidate derived from the 32% misrouting finding (its complement) and asks the PM to confirm both measure the same tickets the same way.

assertions.name: inferred-after-confirmation
assertions.text: The response says that, once confirmed, the baseline is recorded [I] citing the finding with the derivation noted — or keeps it a GAP until confirmation.

assertions.name: one-question
assertions.text: The response asks one question rather than a questionnaire.

evals.evaluation_stage: Mid-flow, panel 3 — the candidate-baseline check with a finding.

evals.name: a-figure-read-off-a-reops-page-is-not-transcribed
evals.prompt: Panel 3, primary metric is average triage time per ticket. I just opened the time study's page in ReOps — it says 1.9 minutes per ticket. Put that in as the baseline.
evals.expected_output: The response does not record 1.9 minutes as [E] or as a transcribed [T] figure: a figure ReOps holds reaches the canvas as a study finding the graph holds, never read off a ReOps page (the verifier refuses a [T] citing a ReOps record). It keeps 1.9 as the PM's assumption beside the evidence GAP ([A]), not used in any calculation. It turns the page into the route: the researcher records the time study's triage-time result as a finding on study-ts-07 in ReOps, the push brings it into the graph, and the next refresh reads it — then it can be the baseline, cited [E], and it is graph-backed. It creates or offers that to-do with the measure (average minutes per ticket spent on triage). It moves on to the target without lecturing.

assertions.name: not-transcribed
assertions.text: 1.9 minutes is not recorded as [E] or [T]; the response says ReOps figures reach the canvas as findings in the graph, not by reading a ReOps page.

assertions.name: kept-as-assumption
assertions.text: The figure is kept visibly as an assumption beside the GAP and is not used in calculations.

assertions.name: record-a-finding-todo
assertions.text: The to-do is for the researcher to record the triage-time result as a finding in ReOps (so it reaches the graph), naming the measure.

assertions.name: moves-forward
assertions.text: The response continues to the next decision (the target) rather than blocking the session.

evals.evaluation_stage: Mid-flow, panel 3 — open question 3 (2026-09-26): no transcription from ReOps.
